items.title: FASCICLE 34 COMPLETE, THE GROUND OF THE HEARER-DISCIPLES CONCLUDES ENTIRELY, AND THE GROUND OF THE SOLITARY BUDDHA OPENS

items.zh: 如是一切名聲聞地。此是一切正等覺者所說一切聲聞相應教法根本，猶如一切名句文身是所制造文章、呪術、異論根本。◎
items.en: All of this together is called the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples. This is the root of every teaching on the hearer-disciples' path spoken by every fully awakened one — just as every collection of words, phrases, and syllables is the root from which composed writings, incantations, and diverse treatises are made.

items.zh: 如是已說聲聞地。云何獨覺地？當知此地有五種相。一者、種姓，二者、道，三者、習，四者、住，五者、行。
items.en: The fourteenth ground within the Basic Section: the Ground of the Solitary Buddha. The Ground of the Hearer-Disciples has now been fully explained. What is the Ground of the Solitary Buddha? One should know this ground has five aspects: lineage, path, habituation, abiding, and conduct.

items.zh: 云何獨覺種姓？謂由三相，應正了知。

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Solitary-Buddha Disposition, and Three Paths to the Same Awakening

items.zh: 一者、本性獨覺，先未證得彼菩提時，有薄塵種姓。由此因緣，於憒鬧處，心不愛樂；於寂靜處，深心愛樂。二者、本性獨覺，先未證得彼菩提時，有薄悲種姓。由是因緣，於說正法利有情事，心不愛樂；於少思務寂靜住中，深心愛樂。三者、本性獨覺，先未證得彼菩提時，有中根種，姓，是慢行類。由是因緣，深心希願無師、無敵而證菩提。
items.en: First, one inherently inclined to solitary awakening, before attaining that awakening, possesses a lineage of thin affliction … second … possesses a lineage of thin compassion … third … possesses a middling lineage, of the pride-inclined type; because of this, one deeply wishes to attain awakening without any teacher and without any rival.

items.zh: 云何獨覺道？謂由三相，應正了知。
謂有一類，安住獨覺種姓，經於百劫，值佛出世，親近承事，成熟相續，專心求證獨覺菩提。於蘊善巧、於處善巧、於界善巧、於緣起善巧、於處非處善巧、於諦善巧勤修學故，於當來世，速能證得獨覺菩提。如是名為初獨覺道。
items.en: There is one kind who, abiding in the solitary-buddha lineage, over a hundred eons repeatedly encounters buddhas arising in the world, draws near and attends them, ripening in continuity, single-mindedly seeking to realise solitary awakening … in a future life, is thereby able to swiftly attain solitary awakening. This is called the first path of the solitary buddha.

items.zh: 復有一類，值佛出世，親近善士，聽聞正法，如理作意，於先所未起順決擇分善根，引發令起，謂煗、頂、忍；而無力能即於此生證法現觀，得沙門果。復修蘊善巧、修處善巧、修界善巧、修緣起善巧、修處非處善巧、修諦善巧故，於當來世能證法現觀，得沙門果。是名第二獨覺道。復有一類，值佛出世，親近善士，聽聞正法，如理作意，證法現觀，得沙門果；而無力能於一切種至極究竟，畢竟離垢，畢竟證得梵行邊際阿羅漢果。復修蘊善巧、修處善巧、修界善巧、修緣起善巧、修處非處善巧、修諦善巧故，依出世道，於當來世至極究竟，畢竟離垢，畢竟證得梵行邊際阿羅漢果。是名第三獨覺道。云何獨覺習？謂有一類，依初獨覺道，滿足百劫修集資糧。過百劫已，出無佛世。無師自能修三十七菩提分法，證法現觀，得獨覺菩提果，永斷一切煩惱，成阿羅漢。復有一類，或依第二、或依第三獨覺道。由彼因緣，出無佛世，無師自能修三十七菩提分法，或證法現觀，乃至得阿羅漢果，或得沙門果，至極究竟，畢竟離垢，畢竟證得梵行邊際，證得最上阿羅漢果。

items.title: FASCICLE 34 FULLY COMPLETE — Habituation, Dwelling, and Conduct Close the Ground of the Solitary Buddha

items.zh: 當知此中，由初習故成獨覺者，名麟角喻。由第二、第三習故成獨勝者，名部行喻。云何獨覺住？謂初所習麟角喻獨覺，樂處孤林，樂獨居住，樂甚深勝解，樂觀察甚深緣起道理，樂安住最極空、無願、無相作意。若第二、第三所習部行喻獨勝，不必一向樂處孤林、樂獨居住，亦樂部眾共相雜住。
items.en: One should know that a solitary buddha formed through the first habituation is called rhinoceros-horn-like; one formed through the second or third habituation is called group-practising-like … the rhinoceros-horn-like solitary buddha, formed through the first habituation, delights in solitary forests, delights in dwelling alone … the group-practising-like ones, formed through the second or third habituation, are also content to dwell mixed together with a community.

items.zh: 所餘住相，如麟角喻。云何獨覺行？
謂一切獨覺，隨依彼彼村邑聚落而住，善護其身、善守諸根、善住正念，隨入彼彼村邑聚落，或為乞食。或濟度他下劣愚昧，以身濟度，不以語言。何以故？唯現身相為彼說法，不發言故。示現種種神通境界，乃至為令心誹謗者生歸向故。又彼一切，應知本來一向趣寂。◎
items.en: Every solitary buddha, dwelling near this or that village or town, well guards the body, well guards the senses, and well abides in mindfulness, entering this or that village or town to beg for alms. They may deliver the lowly and confused, but do so through bodily manifestation, not through speech … they teach solely by manifesting bodily forms, never by uttering words … and all of them, one should know, are from the outset uniformly inclined towards quiescence.

blocks.text: The Śrāvaka Stage, begun on Day 176, ends today. Then the treatise briefly describes the fourteenth stage: the **solitary buddhas** (pratyekabuddha, 獨覺), who awaken without a teacher in an age with no Buddha. A passage (0477c21) is untranslated.
"All this is called the Stage of the Hearers: the root of every teaching on the hearers' path spoken by every Buddha, just as words, phrases, and syllables are the root from which all writing comes."
Five aspects: lineage, path, habituation, abiding, conduct.

Before awakening, one of the solitary-buddha lineage has "thin affliction", "thin compassion" (Venerable Miào Jìng: scant, not absent), and a "middling, pride-inclined" nature: "one deeply wishes to attain awakening without any teacher and without any rival".

One who over a hundred aeons meets Buddhas, serves them, and ripens, aiming at solitary awakening. The untranslated prose (0477c21) gives two more: one who meets a Buddha and develops the stages of warmth, summit, and forbearance, but cannot yet see the truths in this life; and one who sees the truths and attains a fruit, but cannot yet complete arhatship. Each cultivates skill in the aggregates, sense-fields, elements, dependent origination, what is possible, and the truths, and in a later life, "in an age without a Buddha, without a teacher", completes awakening.

One formed through the first path is "like a rhinoceros horn", solitary; those through the second or third "practise in groups". They live near villages, guarding body and senses, and "may deliver the lowly and confused, but through bodily manifestation, not through speech".

Thirteen stages of the treatise's seventeen are now behind us, and with them the longest single stage. Fascicle 35 begins the **Bodhisattva Stage** (菩薩地), the treatise's great account of the Mahāyāna path.

quiz.q: The Hearers' Ground is the root of all hearer teachings, "just as words, phrases, and syllables" are the root of writing. How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: from syllables come words and phrases, and only then writing
quiz.why: "Just as every collection of words, phrases, and syllables is the root from which composed writings, incantations, and diverse treatises are made." Venerable Miào Jìng: relying on syllables one forms words and phrases, and only then can one write.

quiz.q: The second solitary-buddha type "has a lineage of thin compassion." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: not without compassion — just little of it
quiz.why: "Second … possesses a lineage of thin compassion." Venerable Miào Jìng: compassion is scant — not absent, just little.

quiz.q: The pride-inclined type "wishes to attain awakening without teacher or rival." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: hopes to awaken on seeing present conditions — by oneself, self-realised without a teacher
quiz.why: "Because of this, one deeply wishes to attain awakening without any teacher and without any rival." Master Cháng Bǎi: one hopes to attain the fruit on seeing present conditions, achieving solitary awakening by oneself — self-realised without a teacher.

quiz.q: "麟角喻" and "部行喻" — rendered "rhinoceros-horn-like" and "group-practising-like" (merely content to dwell with others). What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: the 麟 is no deer, one-horned, taking no disciples; group-practicers lead others and take disciples; Cháng Bǎi: 部行 means "commander" — they lead a community
quiz.why: "A solitary buddha formed through the first habituation is called rhinoceros-horn-like; one formed through the second or third habituation is called group-practising-like." Venerable Miào Jìng: the 麟 is not a deer — it has one horn, not two; the group-practicer can lead people practising together — that is, take disciples. Master Cháng Bǎi: 部行 means "commander"; such practitioners lead a community. The English "content to dwell mixed together" weakens the sense of leading.

quiz.q: Solitary buddhas deliver others "through the body, not through speech." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: by displaying powers through bodily form, not by verbal teaching
quiz.why: "They may deliver the lowly and confused, but do so through bodily manifestation, not through speech." Master Cháng Bǎi: they all deliver by showing powers through bodily form, not by verbal teaching.
